question: According to North Dakota's school bus equipment standards, what exterior color must every school bus have?
choice_a: Glossy white
choice_b: Glossy yellow
choice_c: Glossy orange
choice_d: Reflective silver
explanation: The manual states each school bus must have the standard school bus glossy yellow color on the exterior.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), School Bus Equipment and Standards

question: How tall must the lettering for the words 'School Bus' be on the front and rear of a North Dakota school bus?
choice_a: Eight inches
choice_b: Four inches
choice_c: Twelve inches
choice_d: Six inches
explanation: The words 'School Bus' in letters eight inches in height must be printed on the front and rear of each school bus.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), School Bus Equipment and Standards

question: What words must appear on a sign on the rear of every North Dakota school bus?
choice_a: "CAUTION: STUDENTS ABOARD"
choice_b: "STOP FOR SCHOOL BUS"
choice_c: "DANGER: DO NOT PASS"
choice_d: "THIS SCHOOL BUS STOPS AT ALL RAILROAD CROSSINGS"
explanation: Every school bus must be equipped with a rear sign containing the words "THIS SCHOOL BUS STOPS AT ALL RAILROAD CROSSINGS."
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), School Bus Equipment and Standards

question: Under North Dakota law, when may studded tires be used on a school bus transporting school children?
choice_a: Only October 15 to April 15
choice_b: Never - they are prohibited on buses
choice_c: At any time during the year
choice_d: Only during declared snow emergencies
explanation: While most vehicles may use studded tires only October 15 to April 15, a school bus may be equipped with studded tires at any time during the year when transporting school children.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), School Bus Equipment and Standards

question: According to the ND CDL manual, how far can the danger zone extend from the front bumper of a school bus?
choice_a: As much as 30 feet, with the first 10 feet being the most dangerous
choice_b: Exactly 15 feet
choice_c: Up to 50 feet
choice_d: Only 5 feet
explanation: The danger zone may extend as much as 30 feet from the front bumper, with the first 10 feet being the most dangerous.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 10.1 — Danger Zones and Use of Mirrors

question: How far do the danger zones extend from the left and right sides of a school bus?
choice_a: 5 feet
choice_b: 20 feet
choice_c: 10 feet
choice_d: 25 feet
explanation: The danger zones extend 10 feet from the left and right sides of the bus.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 10.1 — Danger Zones and Use of Mirrors

question: Which area around a school bus is always considered dangerous because of passing cars?
choice_a: Directly behind the rear bumper
choice_b: The area to the left of the bus
choice_c: The area under the bus
choice_d: The area to the right of the bus
explanation: The area to the left of the bus is always considered dangerous because of passing cars.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 10.1 — Danger Zones and Use of Mirrors

question: How far behind the rear bumper of a school bus does the danger zone extend?
choice_a: 30 feet
choice_b: 5 feet
choice_c: 20 feet
choice_d: 10 feet
explanation: The danger zone extends 10 feet behind the rear bumper of the school bus.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 10.1 — Danger Zones and Use of Mirrors

question: Where are the outside left and right side flat mirrors mounted on a school bus?
choice_a: At the left and right front corners of the bus, at the side or front of the windshield
choice_b: On the rear bumper
choice_c: Above the windshield on the driver's side
choice_d: Below the convex mirrors near the front wheels
explanation: The outside left and right side flat mirrors are mounted at the left and right front corners of the bus at the side or front of the windshield.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 10.1 — Danger Zones and Use of Mirrors

question: When properly adjusted, the outside left and right side flat mirrors should let you see how far behind the bus?
choice_a: 100 feet or two bus lengths
choice_b: 200 feet or four bus lengths
choice_c: 50 feet or one bus length
choice_d: 300 feet or six bus lengths
explanation: Properly adjusted flat mirrors should let you see 200 feet or four bus lengths behind the bus.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 10.1 — Danger Zones and Use of Mirrors

question: How far can the blind spot directly behind a school bus (not covered by the flat mirrors) extend, depending on the width of the bus?
choice_a: Only up to 50 feet
choice_b: Up to 100 feet
choice_c: 50 to 150 feet, and possibly up to 400 feet
choice_d: Never more than 25 feet
explanation: The blind spot behind the bus extends 50 to 150 feet and could extend up to 400 feet depending on the width of the bus.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 10.1 — Danger Zones and Use of Mirrors

question: Where are the outside left and right side convex mirrors located on a school bus?
choice_a: Above the windshield
choice_b: On the rear emergency door
choice_c: At the front bumper
choice_d: Below the outside flat mirrors
explanation: The convex mirrors are located below the outside flat mirrors.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 10.1 — Danger Zones and Use of Mirrors

question: The outside convex mirrors on a school bus should be positioned to show the driver which of the following?
choice_a: The entire side of the bus up to the mirror mounts and at least one traffic lane on either side
choice_b: Only the rear license plate
choice_c: The interior of the bus
choice_d: The area directly under the front bumper only
explanation: The convex mirrors should be positioned to see the entire side of the bus up to the mirror mounts, the front of the rear tires touching the ground, and at least one traffic lane on either side.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 10.1 — Danger Zones and Use of Mirrors

question: What is the primary purpose of the outside left and right side crossover mirrors on a school bus?
choice_a: To monitor students seated inside the bus
choice_b: To view the front bumper 'danger zone' area not visible by direct vision, including the service door and front wheel area
choice_c: To check tire pressure
choice_d: To see traffic directly behind the bus
explanation: Crossover mirrors are used to see the front bumper danger zone directly in front of the bus not visible by direct vision, as well as the service door and front wheel area.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 10.1 — Danger Zones and Use of Mirrors

question: The overhead inside rearview mirror on a school bus is used primarily to do what?
choice_a: View traffic approaching from the rear
choice_b: Check the danger zone at the front bumper
choice_c: Monitor passenger activity inside the bus
choice_d: Check tire wear on the rear tires
explanation: The overhead inside rearview mirror is mounted above the windshield on the driver's side and is used to monitor passenger activity inside the bus.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 10.1 — Danger Zones and Use of Mirrors

question: Who establishes official school bus routes and official school bus stops?
choice_a: The bus driver, at his or her discretion
choice_b: The state highway patrol
choice_c: The bus manufacturer
choice_d: The school district
explanation: Each school district establishes official routes and official school bus stops, and stops should never be changed without written approval from the appropriate school district official.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 10.2 — Loading and Unloading

question: If equipped, when should you activate the alternating flashing amber warning lights when approaching a school bus stop?
choice_a: At least 200 feet, or approximately 5-10 seconds, before the stop
choice_b: At least 500 feet before the stop
choice_c: Only after coming to a complete stop
choice_d: Immediately upon seeing students at the stop, regardless of distance
explanation: Alternating flashing amber warning lights should be activated at least 200 feet or approximately 5-10 seconds before the school bus stop, or as state law requires.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 10.2 — Loading and Unloading

question: About how far before stopping should you turn on the right turn signal indicator when approaching a school bus stop?
choice_a: 400-500 feet, or 8-10 seconds
choice_b: 100-300 feet, or approximately 3-5 seconds
choice_c: 10-20 feet, or 1 second
choice_d: Only when the amber lights are already flashing
explanation: The right turn signal indicator should be turned on about 100-300 feet, or approximately 3-5 seconds, prior to stopping.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 10.2 — Loading and Unloading

question: When stopping to load students, how far away from the students at the designated stop should the front bumper of the school bus be?
choice_a: Right next to the students
choice_b: 25 feet
choice_c: At least 10 feet
choice_d: 50 feet
explanation: The bus should come to a full stop with the front bumper at least 10 feet away from students, forcing them to walk to the bus so the driver has a better view of their movements.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 10.2 — Loading and Unloading

question: What should you do with the transmission and parking brake at each school bus stop?
choice_a: Leave the transmission in Drive with the brake off
choice_b: Only apply the parking brake, leave transmission running
choice_c: Turn off the engine and leave it in gear
choice_d: Place the transmission in Park (or Neutral if no Park position) and set the parking brake
explanation: At each stop, place the transmission in Park, or in Neutral if there is no Park shift point, and set the parking brake.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 10.2 — Loading and Unloading

question: When should you activate the alternating red lights and extend the stop arm when stopping to load students?
choice_a: When traffic is a safe distance from the school bus
choice_b: Only after all students have boarded
choice_c: Immediately after turning on the amber lights, regardless of traffic
choice_d: Only if a student requests it
explanation: Activate alternating red lights when traffic is a safe distance from the school bus and ensure the stop arm is extended.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 10.2 — Loading and Unloading

question: According to the loading procedures, what should students at the bus stop do while waiting for the bus?
choice_a: Line up single file at the edge of the road
choice_b: Wait in a designated location, facing the bus as it approaches
choice_c: Stand behind the bus stop sign out of view
choice_d: Approach the bus as soon as they see it coming
explanation: Students should wait in a designated location for the school bus, facing the bus as it approaches, and board only when signaled by the driver.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 10.2 — Loading and Unloading

question: If you cannot account for a student outside the bus during loading, what should you do?
choice_a: Drive away and report it later
choice_b: Honk the horn repeatedly and wait
choice_c: Secure the bus, take the key, and check around and underneath the bus
choice_d: Call the next stop to ask if the student is there
explanation: If you cannot account for a student outside, secure the bus, take the key, and check around and underneath the bus.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 10.2 — Loading and Unloading

question: If a student drops an object near the bus during loading or unloading, what should the student be told to do?
choice_a: Immediately pick it up before boarding
choice_b: Ask another student to retrieve it
choice_c: Wait for the bus to move forward, then retrieve it
choice_d: Leave the object and move to a point of safety, then try to get the driver's attention to retrieve it
explanation: Students should be told to leave any dropped object and move to a point of safety out of the danger zones, then attempt to get the driver's attention to retrieve the object.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 10.2 — Loading and Unloading

question: After unloading students along a route, how far should students be told to walk away from the side of the bus?
choice_a: At least 10 feet
choice_b: At least 25 feet
choice_c: At least 3 feet
choice_d: At least 50 feet
explanation: Students should exit the bus and walk at least 10 feet away from the side of the bus to a position where the driver can plainly see all students.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 10.2 — Loading and Unloading

question: Why should the driver count students while unloading along the route?
choice_a: To keep a record for the school district's payroll
choice_b: To confirm the location of all students before pulling away from the stop
choice_c: To determine how many seats are empty
choice_d: It is not necessary to count students
explanation: The driver should count the number of students while unloading to confirm the location of all students before pulling away from the stop.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 10.2 — Loading and Unloading

question: When a student must cross the roadway in front of the bus, to what position should the student walk before stopping?
choice_a: Directly behind the bus
choice_b: Only to the edge of the bus's shadow
choice_c: At least 10 feet in front of the right corner of the bumper, while remaining away from the front of the bus
choice_d: Onto the roadway immediately
explanation: The student should walk to a location at least 10 feet in front of the right corner of the bumper, while still remaining away from the front of the school bus.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 10.2 — Loading and Unloading

question: Before crossing the roadway on the driver's signal, where should a student stop and look again?
choice_a: In the middle of the roadway
choice_b: At the rear of the bus
choice_c: Behind the stop sign
choice_d: At the left edge of the school bus
explanation: Students should cross far enough in front of the bus to be in the driver's view, stop at the left edge of the school bus, and look again for the driver's signal to continue crossing.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 10.2 — Loading and Unloading

question: When unloading students at the school, what should the driver do before leaving the bus unattended?
choice_a: Turn off the ignition switch and remove the key if leaving the driver's compartment
choice_b: Leave the engine running for the next trip
choice_c: Leave the key in the ignition for the next driver
choice_d: Set only the parking brake and leave the engine idling
explanation: When unloading at school, the driver should secure the bus by turning off the ignition switch and removing the key if leaving the driver's compartment.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 10.2 — Loading and Unloading

question: During the post-trip inspection, the driver should walk through and around the bus checking for which of the following?
choice_a: Only the fuel gauge reading
choice_b: Sleeping students, articles left on the bus, open windows/doors, and damage or vandalism
choice_c: The bus's total mileage only
choice_d: Only the tire pressure
explanation: The post-trip inspection includes checking for articles left on the bus, sleeping students, open windows and doors, mechanical/operational problems, and damage or vandalism.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 10.2 — Loading and Unloading

question: What is described as the first and most important consideration in deciding how to handle a bus emergency?
choice_a: Calling 911 immediately
choice_b: Turning on the hazard lights
choice_c: Recognizing the hazard
choice_d: Evacuating all students immediately
explanation: The first and most important consideration is for the driver to recognize the hazard.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 10.3 — Emergency Exit and Evacuation

question: As a general rule, student safety and control during an emergency is best maintained by doing what?
choice_a: Evacuating immediately in every situation
choice_b: Having students exit through windows only
choice_c: Calling for a police escort before doing anything else
choice_d: Keeping students on the bus, if doing so does not expose them to unnecessary risk or injury
explanation: As a general rule, student safety and control is best maintained by keeping students on the bus during an emergency, if that does not expose them to unnecessary risk or injury.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 10.3 — Emergency Exit and Evacuation

question: Which of the following is listed as a condition requiring mandatory evacuation of a school bus?
choice_a: The bus is stalled on or adjacent to a railroad-highway crossing
choice_b: The bus's ABS malfunction lamp is illuminated
choice_c: A single student is misbehaving
choice_d: The bus is running 10 minutes behind schedule
explanation: The driver must evacuate the bus when it is stalled on or adjacent to a railroad-highway crossing, among other mandatory conditions.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 10.3 — Emergency Exit and Evacuation

question: Besides fire and railroad crossing hazards, which of these also requires a mandatory evacuation?
choice_a: Heavy rain
choice_b: An imminent danger of collision
choice_c: A flat tire
choice_d: A broken radio
explanation: The driver must evacuate the bus when there is an imminent danger of collision, among other mandatory conditions.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 10.3 — Emergency Exit and Evacuation

question: According to the manual, how far off the road should a 'safe place' be located, in the direction of oncoming traffic?
choice_a: At least 25 feet
choice_b: At least 50 feet
choice_c: At least 100 feet
choice_d: At least 500 feet
explanation: A safe place will be at least 100 feet off the road in the direction of oncoming traffic, to keep students from being hit by debris if another vehicle collides with the bus.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 10.3 — Emergency Exit and Evacuation

question: If fire is present during an evacuation, in which direction should students be led?
choice_a: Downwind of the bus
choice_b: Toward the fire to assess it
choice_c: Directly behind the bus
choice_d: Upwind of the bus
explanation: The manual instructs drivers to lead students upwind of the bus if fire is present.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 10.3 — Emergency Exit and Evacuation

question: If there is a risk from spilled hazardous materials during an evacuation, how far upwind of the bus should students be led?
choice_a: At least 300 feet
choice_b: At least 50 feet
choice_c: At least 100 feet
choice_d: At least 1,000 feet
explanation: Students should be led upwind of the bus at least 300 feet if there is a risk from spilled hazardous materials.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 10.3 — Emergency Exit and Evacuation

question: If the bus is in the direct path of a sighted tornado and evacuation is ordered, what should students be directed to do if no building shelter is available?
choice_a: Remain seated on the bus with seatbelts fastened
choice_b: Lie face down in a nearby ditch or culvert with hands covering their heads
choice_c: Stand in a tight group next to the bus
choice_d: Run in the direction the tornado is moving
explanation: If the bus is in the direct path of a sighted tornado, escort students to a nearby ditch or culvert if a building is not available, and direct them to lie face down with hands covering their heads.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 10.3 — Emergency Exit and Evacuation

question: During an evacuation, when should a student believed to have a neck or spinal injury be moved?
choice_a: Immediately, regardless of the situation
choice_b: Only by another student
choice_c: Only if his or her life is in immediate danger
choice_d: Never, under any circumstance
explanation: Do not move a student believed to have suffered a neck or spinal injury unless his or her life is in immediate danger.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 10.3 — Emergency Exit and Evacuation

question: As part of securing the bus during an evacuation, what should the driver do with the engine and ignition key?
choice_a: Leave the engine running and the key in the ignition
choice_b: Leave the engine running but remove the key
choice_c: Turn off the engine but leave the key in the ignition
choice_d: Shut off the engine and remove the ignition key
explanation: Securing the bus includes setting the parking brake, shutting off the engine, and removing the ignition key.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 10.3 — Emergency Exit and Evacuation

question: If the radio is inoperable during an evacuation and help is needed, what does the manual describe as a last resort?
choice_a: Dispatching two older, responsible students to go for help
choice_b: Waiting silently for a passerby to notice
choice_c: Having the youngest student flag down traffic
choice_d: Abandoning the bus and walking to the nearest town
explanation: As a last resort, the driver should dispatch two older, responsible students to go for help if there is no working radio.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 10.3 — Emergency Exit and Evacuation

question: What characterizes a 'passive' railroad-highway crossing?
choice_a: It has flashing red lights and gates
choice_b: It does not have any type of traffic control device
choice_c: It only occurs on multi-lane highways
choice_d: It is reserved for freight trains only
explanation: A passive crossing does not have any type of traffic control device; the decision to proceed rests entirely with the driver.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 10.4 — Railroad-Highway Crossings

question: What distinguishes an 'active' railroad-highway crossing from a passive one?
choice_a: Active crossings have no warning signs at all
choice_b: Active crossings are only found in cities
choice_c: Active crossings have a traffic control device, such as flashing lights or gates
choice_d: Active crossings never require a full stop
explanation: Active crossings have a traffic control device installed to regulate traffic, including flashing red lights, bells, and/or gates.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 10.4 — Railroad-Highway Crossings

question: What does the round, black-on-yellow advance warning sign placed ahead of a railroad crossing tell the driver to do?
choice_a: Speed up to clear the crossing before a train arrives
choice_b: Ignore it if no train is visible
choice_c: Sound the horn continuously
choice_d: Slow down, look and listen for the train, and be prepared to stop
explanation: The advance warning sign tells the driver to slow down, look and listen for the train, and be prepared to stop at the tracks if a train is coming.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 10.4 — Railroad-Highway Crossings

question: Pavement markings at a railroad crossing typically consist of what?
choice_a: An "X" with the letters "RR" and a no-passing marking
choice_b: A solid white stop bar only
choice_c: A yellow diamond with a train silhouette
choice_d: Diagonal red and white stripes
explanation: Pavement markings consist of an "X" with the letters "RR" and a no-passing marking on two-lane roads.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 10.4 — Railroad-Highway Crossings

question: If there is a white stop line painted on the pavement before railroad tracks, where must the front of the school bus remain while stopped?
choice_a: On top of the stop line
choice_b: Behind the stop line
choice_c: At least 5 feet past the stop line
choice_d: It does not matter as long as the bus is stopped
explanation: The front of the school bus must remain behind the white stop line while stopped at the crossing.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 10.4 — Railroad-Highway Crossings

question: If there is no white stop line painted on the pavement at a crossbuck-marked crossing, where must the bus stop?
choice_a: At the nearest rail
choice_b: 100 feet before the crossbuck
choice_c: Before the crossbuck sign
choice_d: It may proceed without stopping if the tracks appear clear
explanation: If there is no white line painted on the pavement, the driver must stop the bus before the crossbuck sign.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 10.4 — Railroad-Highway Crossings

question: When the flashing red lights at a railroad crossing begin to flash, what must the driver do?
choice_a: Proceed cautiously without stopping
choice_b: Sound the horn and continue
choice_c: Wait for a gate to appear before stopping
choice_d: Stop, because a train is approaching and the driver must yield the right-of-way
explanation: When the lights begin to flash, the driver must stop because a train is approaching, and must yield the right-of-way to the train.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 10.4 — Railroad-Highway Crossings

question: If the gate at a railroad crossing stays down after the train has passed, what should the driver do?
choice_a: Not drive around the gate; instead, call the dispatcher
choice_b: Drive around the gate carefully
choice_c: Wait exactly 60 seconds, then proceed
choice_d: Honk the horn until the gate rises
explanation: If the gate stays down after the train passes, the driver should not drive around it and should instead call the dispatcher.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 10.4 — Railroad-Highway Crossings

question: What is the Emergency Notification System (ENS) at a railroad crossing used for?
choice_a: Automatically stopping trains when a bus is present
choice_b: Reporting obstructions or malfunctioning lights/gates via a posted phone number
choice_c: Alerting the school district that the bus is running late
choice_d: Notifying passengers of the next scheduled stop
explanation: The Federal Railroad Administration posts emergency phone numbers on crossing posts or control boxes; drivers call this number to report obstructions or malfunctioning lights or gates.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 10.4 — Railroad-Highway Crossings

question: When stopping at a railroad crossing, how close and how far can the bus stop from the nearest rail?
choice_a: No closer than 5 feet and no farther than 20 feet
choice_b: Exactly at the rail
choice_c: No closer than 15 feet and no farther than 50 feet
choice_d: No closer than 50 feet and no farther than 100 feet
explanation: The driver should stop no closer than 15 feet and no farther than 50 feet from the nearest rail, where there is the best view of the tracks.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 10.4 — Railroad-Highway Crossings

question: At the crossing, after stopping, what should the driver do before proceeding?
choice_a: Immediately shift into a higher gear
choice_b: Close all windows and turn up the radio
choice_c: Honk the horn three times
choice_d: Turn off radios and noisy equipment, silence passengers, and open the service door and driver's window to look and listen
explanation: At the crossing, the driver should turn off radios and noisy equipment, silence passengers, and open the service door and driver's window to look and listen for an approaching train.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 10.4 — Railroad-Highway Crossings

question: At a multiple-track crossing, once the driver is sure no train is approaching on any track, how should the bus proceed?
choice_a: Proceed across all tracks in a low gear without changing gears until completely clear
choice_b: Stop again between each set of tracks
choice_c: Change to a higher gear halfway across
choice_d: Reverse back off the tracks periodically to check for trains
explanation: At a multiple-track crossing, once sure no train is approaching on any track, the driver should proceed across all tracks in a low gear until completely clear, without changing gears.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 10.4 — Railroad-Highway Crossings

question: If a school bus stalls or becomes trapped on railroad tracks, what should the driver do?
choice_a: Stay on the bus and wait for help
choice_b: Get everyone out and move away from the bus at an angle away from the tracks and toward the train
choice_c: Try to push the bus off the tracks
choice_d: Wait for a police officer before evacuating
explanation: If the bus stalls or is trapped on the tracks, get everyone out and off the tracks immediately, moving everyone away from the bus at an angle away from the tracks and toward the train.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 10.4 — Railroad-Highway Crossings

question: If a behavior problem occurs on the bus during loading or unloading, what should the driver do?
choice_a: Address it immediately while students are still boarding
choice_b: Stop the bus mid-route regardless of surrounding traffic
choice_c: Wait until unloading students are safely off and have moved away, then handle the problem if necessary
choice_d: Ignore it until the end of the route
explanation: If a behavior problem occurs, wait until students unloading are safely off the bus and have moved away; pull the bus over to handle the problem if necessary.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 10.5 — Student Management

question: When handling a serious problem on the bus, where should the driver park the bus?
choice_a: In the travel lane with hazards on
choice_b: On a bridge or overpass
choice_c: At the next scheduled stop only
choice_d: In a safe location off the road, such as a parking lot or driveway
explanation: The driver should stop the bus and park in a safe location off the road, perhaps a parking lot or a driveway.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 10.5 — Student Management

question: What tone does the manual recommend a driver use when speaking to an offending student?
choice_a: Respectful and courteous, but firm, without showing anger
choice_b: Loud and stern to assert authority
choice_c: Silent, ignoring the student entirely
choice_d: Apologetic, to avoid conflict
explanation: The driver should speak respectfully in a courteous manner with a firm voice, without showing anger, while making clear that he or she means business.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 10.5 — Student Management

question: If a change of seating is needed to manage a student's behavior, what does the manual recommend?
choice_a: Moving the student to the very back of the bus
choice_b: Requesting the student move to a seat near the driver
choice_c: Having the student stand for the remainder of the trip
choice_d: Removing the student from the bus at the next intersection
explanation: If a change of seating is needed, the driver should request that the student move to a seat near the driver.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 10.5 — Student Management

question: Other than in a true emergency, where is a student allowed to be put off the bus?
choice_a: Anywhere the driver deems appropriate
choice_b: At the nearest gas station
choice_c: At school or at the student's designated school bus stop
choice_d: At any location a parent requests
explanation: A driver should never put a student off the bus except at school or at his or her designated school bus stop.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 10.5 — Student Management

question: If an offense is serious enough that the driver cannot safely drive the bus, what should the driver do?
choice_a: Continue driving and report it at the end of the shift
choice_b: Physically remove the student from the seat
choice_c: Speed to the nearest school
choice_d: Call for a school administrator or the police to come remove the student
explanation: If the offense is serious enough that the driver cannot safely drive the bus, the driver should call for a school administrator or the police to come and remove the student.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 10.5 — Student Management

question: The Department of Transportation requires antilock braking systems on air brake vehicles (trucks, buses, trailers, and converter dollies) built on or after what date?
choice_a: March 1, 1998
choice_b: January 1, 2000
choice_c: March 1, 1999
choice_d: July 1, 1995
explanation: The DOT requires ABS on air brake vehicles (trucks, buses, trailers, and converter dollies) built on or after March 1, 1998.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 10.6 — Antilock Braking Systems

question: Hydraulically braked trucks and buses with a gross vehicle weight rating of 10,000 pounds or more must have ABS if built on or after what date?
choice_a: March 1, 1998
choice_b: March 1, 1999
choice_c: January 1, 1997
choice_d: March 1, 2000
explanation: Hydraulically braked trucks and buses with a GVWR of 10,000 pounds or more built on or after March 1, 1999 are required to have ABS.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 10.6 — Antilock Braking Systems

question: Where is the yellow ABS malfunction lamp located on a school bus equipped with ABS?
choice_a: On the dashboard of the escort vehicle
choice_b: Above the rear emergency door
choice_c: On the instrument panel
choice_d: On the exterior of the bus near the wheel wells
explanation: A school bus equipped with ABS will have a yellow ABS malfunction lamp on the instrument panel.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 10.6 — Antilock Braking Systems

question: When you brake hard on a slippery surface in a vehicle without ABS, what can happen?
choice_a: The vehicle automatically slows to a safe speed
choice_b: Nothing different happens compared to ABS-equipped vehicles
choice_c: The ABS malfunction lamp illuminates
choice_d: Your wheels may lock up, causing loss of steering control or a skid
explanation: When braking hard on slippery surfaces without ABS, wheels may lock up; if steering wheels lock up, steering control is lost, and other locked wheels can cause a skid or spin.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 10.6 — Antilock Braking Systems

question: What does ABS primarily help a driver do?
choice_a: Avoid wheel lock-up and maintain steering control while braking
choice_b: Stop in a significantly shorter distance every time
choice_c: Brake less often
choice_d: Increase overall braking power
explanation: ABS helps drivers avoid wheel lock-up and maintain control, allowing steering around an obstacle while braking.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 10.6 — Antilock Braking Systems

question: According to the manual, does ABS necessarily shorten stopping distance?
choice_a: Yes, always by at least 25%
choice_b: No, ABS will help maintain control but won't necessarily shorten stopping distance
choice_c: Yes, but only on dry pavement
choice_d: No, ABS always increases stopping distance
explanation: ABS won't necessarily shorten stopping distance; it will help maintain vehicle control.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 10.6 — Antilock Braking Systems

question: In emergency braking on a bus equipped with ABS, what should the driver avoid doing?
choice_a: Applying the brakes at all
choice_b: Steering around obstacles
choice_c: Pumping the brakes
choice_d: Releasing the accelerator
explanation: In emergency braking, the driver should not pump the brakes on a bus with ABS.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 10.6 — Antilock Braking Systems

topic: Braking if ABS is Not Working
question: If the ABS malfunction lamp indicates that ABS is not working, what should the driver do?
choice_a: Immediately pull over and refuse to drive the bus
choice_b: Disconnect the brake system
choice_c: Brake only with the parking brake
choice_d: Drive and brake as normal, since regular brake functions still work, and get the system serviced soon
explanation: If ABS malfunctions, the driver still has regular brakes and should drive normally, but get the system serviced soon.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 10.6 — Antilock Braking Systems

question: According to the manual's safety reminders, what does ABS NOT compensate for?
choice_a: Bad brakes or poor brake maintenance
choice_b: Wet pavement conditions
choice_c: Turning corners
choice_d: Downhill grades
explanation: ABS won't compensate for bad brakes or poor brake maintenance; the best vehicle safety feature is still a safe driver.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 10.6 — Antilock Braking Systems

question: When should the roof-mounted white strobe light on a school bus be used, if the bus is so equipped?
choice_a: Continuously, at all times while driving
choice_b: When visibility is limited, such that the driver cannot easily see in front, behind, or beside the bus
choice_c: Only when loading students at school
choice_d: Only during railroad crossings
explanation: The overhead strobe light should be used when the driver has limited visibility and cannot easily see around the bus.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 10.7 — Special Safety Considerations

question: The manual compares the side of a school bus in strong winds to what?
choice_a: An anchor
choice_b: A parachute
choice_c: A sail on a sailboat
choice_d: A kite
explanation: The manual states that the side of a school bus acts like a sail on a sailboat in strong winds.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 10.7 — Special Safety Considerations

question: If caught in strong winds while driving a school bus, what should the driver do?
choice_a: Speed up to get through the windy area quickly
choice_b: Open the windows to reduce wind resistance
choice_c: Drive in the center of the road straddling the lane line
choice_d: Slow down or pull off the roadway and wait, while keeping a strong grip on the steering wheel
explanation: If caught in strong winds, the driver should keep a strong grip on the steering wheel, anticipate gusts, and slow down or pull off the roadway and wait.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 10.7 — Special Safety Considerations

question: According to the manual, when should you never back a school bus?
choice_a: When students are outside of the bus
choice_b: When it is raining
choice_c: At night
choice_d: On a downhill grade
explanation: The manual states you should never back a school bus when students are outside of the bus.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 10.7 — Special Safety Considerations

question: What is the purpose of posting a lookout when backing a school bus?
choice_a: To operate the bus's mirrors remotely
choice_b: To warn the driver about obstacles, approaching persons, and other vehicles (not to give directions)
choice_c: To direct the exact steering angle needed
choice_d: To count students as they exit
explanation: The purpose of the lookout is to warn the driver about obstacles, approaching persons, and other vehicles; the lookout should not give directions on how to back the bus.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 10.7 — Special Safety Considerations

question: If no lookout is available when a school bus must back up, what should the driver do first?
choice_a: Back up slowly without checking anything
choice_b: Ask a student to serve as lookout instead
choice_c: Set the parking brake, turn off the motor, take the keys, and walk to the rear to check that the way is clear
choice_d: Rely solely on the overhead rearview mirror
explanation: If no lookout is available, the driver should set the parking brake, turn off the motor and take the keys, and walk to the rear of the bus to determine whether the way is clear.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 10.7 — Special Safety Considerations

question: How much tail swing can a school bus have during a turning movement?
choice_a: Up to one foot
choice_b: Up to six feet
choice_c: None; buses have no tail swing
choice_d: Up to three feet
explanation: A school bus can have up to a three-foot tail swing, so drivers must check mirrors before and during turning movements.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 10.7 — Special Safety Considerations
